title: shinyDSP tutorial
text: shinyDSP: Analyzing Visualizing Nanostring GeoMx DSP Data shinyDSP intuitive Shiny application designed comprehensive analysis visualization Nanostring GeoMxDSP data. Users can upload either demo custom datasets, consisting count sample annotation tables. app prompts users select variables interest, potential batch effects, confounding factors, allowing customized exploration. shinyDSP, users can create x-y scatter plots combination categorical variables apply user-defined cutoffs filter samples. app utilizes R package, standR (Liu et al. 2024), perform normalization using methods CPM, upper quartile (Q3), RUV4 (Remove Unwanted Variation). Users can visualize PCA plots generated normalization method, color-coded chosen variables batch. selecting normalization scheme, users can identify differentially expressed genes specified biological groups using limma-voom (Ritchie et al. 2015). app provides “raw” output numbers tables, generates volcano plots pairwise comparisons, displays heatmaps top differentially expressed genes. shinyDSP aims provide robust, start--finish analysis GeoMx data, producing publication-ready outputs easily customizable meet individual aesthetic preferences.

title: shinyDSP internal data processing pipeline explained
text: human kidney data Nanostring loaded ExperimentHub(). Two files required: count matrix matching annotation file. Let’s read files. Time code chunk run: 2.51 seconds
code: library(standR) library(SummarizedExperiment) library(ExperimentHub) library(readr) library(dplyr) library(stats)  eh <- ExperimentHub() AnnotationHub::query(eh, "standR") ## ExperimentHub with 3 records ## # snapshotDate(): 2025-04-12 ## # $dataprovider: Nanostring ## # $species: NA ## # $rdataclass: data.frame ## # additional mcols(): taxonomyid, genome, description, ## #   coordinate_1_based, maintainer, rdatadateadded, preparerclass, tags, ## #   rdatapath, sourceurl, sourcetype  ## # retrieve records with, e.g., 'object[["EH7364"]]'  ##  ##            title                    ##   EH7364 | GeomxDKDdata_count       ##   EH7365 | GeomxDKDdata_sampleAnno  ##   EH7366 | GeomxDKDdata_featureAnno countFilePath <- eh[["EH7364"]] sampleAnnoFilePath <- eh[["EH7365"]]  countFile <- readr::read_delim(unname(countFilePath), na = character()) sampleAnnoFile <- readr::read_delim(unname(sampleAnnoFilePath), na = character())

text: Regions interest(ROIs) can filtered based quantitative variable colData(spe) (colnames(new_sampleAnnoFile)). options can found “QC” nav panel’s side bar. Let’s say want keep ROIs whose “SequencingSaturation” least 85. Time code chunk run: 0.02 seconds can see 14 ROIs filtered .

title: shinyDSP internal data processing pipeline explained
text: Two PCA plots (colour-coded biological groups batch) three normalization schemes automatically created “PCA” nav panel. Let’s take Q3 RUV4 normalization example. Time code chunk run: 0.64 seconds Time code chunk run: 3.04 seconds , .PCAFunction() called generate plot. can see biological replicates group better RUV4 (top) compared Q3 (bottom).  Time code chunk run: 0.27 seconds
code: speQ3 <- standR::geomxNorm(filtered_spe, method = "upperquartile") speQ3 <- scater::runPCA(filtered_spe)  speQ3_compute <- SingleCellExperiment::reducedDim(speQ3, "PCA") speRuv_NCGs <- standR::findNCGs(filtered_spe,         batch_name = "SlideName",         top_n = 200)   speRuvBatchCorrection <- standR::geomxBatchCorrection(speRuv_NCGs,             factors = "disease_region",             NCGs = S4Vectors::metadata(speRuv_NCGs)$NCGs, k = 2         )  speRuv <- scater::runPCA(speRuvBatchCorrection)  speRuv_compute <- SingleCellExperiment::reducedDim(speRuv, "PCA") .PCAFunction(speRuv, speRuv_compute, "disease_region", selectedTypes, c(21,22,23,24), c("blue","dodgerblue1","black","grey75")) .PCAFunction(speQ3, speQ3_compute, "disease_region", selectedTypes, c(21,22,23,24), c("blue","dodgerblue1","black","grey75"))

text: Let’s proceed RUV4 normalization. design matrix created next. Time code chunk run: 0.01 seconds confounding variables chosen main side bar, added model.matrix ~0 + disease_region + confounder1 + confounder2).
code: design <- model.matrix(~0+disease_region+ruv_W1+ruv_W2, data = colData(speRuv))  # Clean up column name colnames(design) <- gsub("disease_region", "", colnames(design))

text: edgeR used convert SpatialExperiment DGEList, filter estimate dispersion. Time code chunk run: 11.72 seconds
code: library(edgeR) dge <- SE2DGEList(speRuv) keep <- filterByExpr(dge, design)  dge <- dge[keep, , keep.lib.sizes = FALSE]  dge <- estimateDisp(dge, design = design, robust = TRUE)

what: Fitting a linear regression model with limma
title: shinyDSP internal data processing pipeline explained
text: app uses duplicateCorrelation() “[s]ince need make comparisons within subjects, necessary treat Patient random effect” limma user’s guide (Ritchie et al. 2015). limma-voom method used standR package recommends (Liu et al. 2024). Time code chunk run: 47.98 seconds
code: library(limma) block_by <- colData(speRuv)[["SlideName"]]  v <- voom(dge, design) corfit <- duplicateCorrelation(v, design,     block = block_by )  v2 <- voom(dge, design,     block = block_by,     correlation = corfit$consensus )  corfit2 <- duplicateCorrelation(v, design,     block = block_by )  fit <- lmFit(v, design,     block = block_by,     correlation = corfit2$consensus )  fit_contrast <- contrasts.fit(fit,     contrasts = con )  efit <- eBayes(fit_contrast, robust = TRUE)

title: shinyDSP internal data processing pipeline explained
text: contrast (column con), app creates table top differentially expressed genes sorted adjusted P value. Time code chunk run: 0.03 seconds topTabDF now list tables list index corresponds columns con. tables shown user “Tables” nav panel.

title: shinyDSP: A Shiny App For Visualizing Nanostring GeoMx DSP Data — shinyDSP-package
text: package Shiny app interactively analyzing visualizing Nanostring GeoMX Whole Transcriptome Atlas data. Users option exploring sample data explore app's functionality. Regions interest (ROIs) can filtered based user-provided metadata. Upon taking two groups interest, pairwise ANOVA-like testing automatically performed. Available ouputs include PCA, Volcano plots, tables heatmaps. Aesthetics output highly customizable.
